aus.claim: The internal grievance procedure provided by the Act is, in general terms, an adequate alternate remedy which must be exhausted before initiating proceedings in the Federal Court.
aus.limits: This applies where the respondent raises a preliminary point that the applicant has not exhausted internal remedies, rendering the application premature.

evidence.quote:
There is authority in this Court in the form of  
 Fortin v. Établissement de Donnacona (Directeur) 
 , [1997] F.C.J. No. 138; 153 F.T.R. 84 (T.D.), a decision of Teitelbaum, J., and  
  <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> ; 148 F.T.R. 81 (T.D.), a decision of Rosthstein, J. (as he then was), that the internal grievance procedure provided by the  
 Act 
  is, in general terms, an adequate alternate remedy which must be exhausted before initiating proceedings in the Federal Court.

aus.claim: The underlying rationale is that the statutory remedy is deprived of any relevance if it can simply be bypassed in favour of the Federal Court.
